name: run_inspect
description: Read public details or upgrade previews relevant to the current non-combat decision, such as owned cards, relics, potions, map options, rewards, shop offers, or event choices. Use the latest state and observed history first; query when a missing detail could change your plan. Use supplied references and supported areas. This tool does not purchase, claim, upgrade, or advance the game. Upgrade previews are hypothetical; current observations take precedence over old details. The result includes the current state and requested details in data. Use area=state to read the current public state, without refs or upgrade; this returns no separate query data. To reread details, inspect the relevant area and supplied references; requested content is returned in data even if previously read. Omit refs to inspect the whole area. Use options for offered operations and selection candidates. A detail request whose public state changes while it is read fails rather than combining mismatched observations. Unknown or unavailable values are not zero. No hidden order or hidden values are revealed. Public query areas are shared by Run and Combat; availability follows the current game state. An explicit upgrade inspection returns the current live details and a separate data.upgrades entry keyed by the card reference, containing the complete hypothetical next-upgrade version. Compare those entries directly; no separate before copy or numeric difference is supplied. Not upgradable and unavailable preview are distinct. A read failure is reported as a failure, not hidden as missing data. Hypothetical values never replace current live values. Requested refs must be distinct current public members of the requested area. If any reference is not in that area, the entire detail query fails and identifies the invalid references; it does not omit entries, change areas, or match by name. A trustworthy current state is still returned when available. Omit refs to read the whole area; an empty list is invalid. state, map, combat_history, and powers do not accept refs. Unknown fields on a valid object remain distinct from an invalid reference. Areas are state, map, combat_history, hand, draw, discard, exhaust, other, deck, options, rewards, shop, relics, potions, powers, and enemies. combat_history reads the current battle public card history, not cross-battle reports. Upgrade previews apply to cards in a card-containing area; other object details remain current facts. For powers, omit refs; the result covers all currently relevant holders. Use enemies with enemy references to inspect particular enemies.

name: run_knowledge
description: Look up native game definitions and any configured supplementary knowledge relevant to run planning, including objects not currently owned. Use this for rules and explanations; use run_inspect for current offers, instances, or upgrade previews. Generic definitions do not override live prices, eligibility, or instance effects. This is a read-only query. The result includes the current state and requested knowledge in data. Use mode=catalog to discover supported categories and filter values, mode=search for concise matches, and mode=lookup for full entries. Search filters apply to base definitions, not live objects. Combine different card filters with AND and alternatives within a filter with OR. An empty matches list means no match; missing lookup IDs are reported individually. Explicit lookups always return their text. Query pagination does not preserve a snapshot across catalog changes. This tool never advances the game. Search uses case-insensitive substring matching of whitespace-separated terms against native IDs, localized names, and base definition text; every term must match. Without spaces, a phrase is one substring. Exact ID or name matches rank first, then matches whose terms all occur in the ID or name, then text matches; ties use native ID order. Filters are not relaxed, and supplementary text does not select native matches. Search defaults to 5 results and accepts at most 20; use a larger limit for broad screening. total reports the match count; next_offset is null when no next page exists. Each search match includes the native definition ID, localized name, and complete native base description. Card matches also include confirmed base type, rarity, and cost. Search does not add private strategy text or generated summaries; use lookup for complete entries and configured supplements. Search category is optional: omit it to search all supported categories, or supply it to restrict results strictly. Each match includes its category. Card filters require category=card. Card filters use pools, types, rarities, and energy_costs. Pool, type, and rarity values come from catalog; they are not assumed to be native definition IDs. Catalog identifies each character's own card pool; this does not mean every card that character could obtain. energy_costs matches unupgraded base energy costs, using non-negative integers or "X", never current combat costs. Different dimensions combine with AND; alternatives within a dimension combine with OR. Omit a dimension to leave it unconstrained. Empty lists, duplicates, and unknown filter values are input errors, not empty matches. lookup accepts 1 to 20 distinct native IDs. entries contains found full entries in request order; missing_ids lists IDs absent from the native catalog in request order. Missing supplementary knowledge does not make a native definition missing. Catalog or enabled-extension failures are reported as failures, not missing IDs or empty supplements. A card lookup includes its complete base definition after the next upgrade, without recursively expanding further upgrades. Search still returns the base version. These encyclopedia values exclude live instance modifiers; inspect supplies actual instance values. Non-card entries have no upgrade version. A native definition that cannot upgrade is distinguished from an unavailable preview; actual read failures remain failures.

category.description: Supported category from catalog; omitted searches all categories.

text.description: Whitespace-separated, case-insensitive substring terms; all terms must match.

filters.description: Card filters use pools, types, rarities, and energy_costs. Pool, type, and rarity values come from catalog; they are not assumed to be native definition IDs. Catalog identifies each character's own card pool; this does not mean every card that character could obtain. energy_costs matches unupgraded base energy costs, using non-negative integers or "X", never current combat costs. Different dimensions combine with AND; alternatives within a dimension combine with OR. Omit a dimension to leave it unconstrained. Empty lists, duplicates, and unknown filter values are input errors, not empty matches.

name: run_skill
description: Read task guidance and associated resources relevant to non-combat decisions and run planning. Request guidance when needed and reuse already available guidance while it remains applicable. Reading guidance does not select a route, execute game actions, or start another agent. The result includes the current state and requested guidance in data. Use mode=list to discover configured guidance and mode=read with its exact id to read it. To read an associated resource, also supply a resource key advertised by that guidance. Do not construct filesystem paths. No configured guidance yields an empty list; a load failure is an error, not an empty result. An unknown id or resource returns rejected; a real read failure returns failed. Explicit reads return the requested text even if it was read before. Guidance does not override tool contracts or authorize hidden information. List entries contain id, name, and a short description. Read returns the requested full text and advertised resource keys with short descriptions; an entry with no associated resources has an empty resource list. The list does not expand full texts or expose filesystem paths.

resource.description: Resource key advertised by this skill; never a filesystem path.

name: combat_act
description:
Submit ordered steps: play_card with card and a target when required; use_potion with potion and a target when required; discard_potion with potion; end_turn; select with refs; or interact with a listed action reference. Use interact only for other offered operations; direct actions are not duplicated as interact choices. Execute game actions and selections in the current battle. Use this tool to play cards, use available combat items, resolve combat choices, or end the turn. Prefer one ordered sequence for actions, anticipated selections, and follow-up plays that you can plan from public information. This tool performs the submitted steps; it does not delegate the rest of the battle to another agent.

Displayed costs and effect previews describe the state before the first step, within any shown target scope. Predict later costs, damage, block, and other effects from earlier steps and the rules and current states of cards, relics, enemies, and powers. Account for triggers, counters, and effects consumed by earlier actions. A preview for one target is not a promise for a different target or later state.

Use current pile lists for membership and observed history for relevant prior effects. Identify desired selection options and their supplied references before submitting a sequence. Use combat_inspect first if a missing public detail would change your choice. Include the triggering action, anticipated selection, and follow-up plays together when public information supports them. Use references exactly as supplied, not list positions or invented IDs. Pile lists do not reveal hidden draw order.

Steps run in the submitted order and are checked against the actual state when reached. A later step may become legal because of an earlier step. Selections must satisfy the actual candidates and required count. Steps that remain valid across possible random outcomes may be combined. If an unknown result would change your choice, submit through the revealing action and decide from its result. A draw needs no stop when the remaining steps stay appropriate whatever is drawn.

The result reports outcome and the current state after execution settles. completed means the submitted operation finished, not that the battle was won. If a step is invalid or needs a new decision, execution stops and reports the completed prefix, stopping reason, and suggested next actions; completed effects are not undone. Continue from that state without replaying completed steps. If execution is unknown, submit no actions until a fresh state reports control=ready; read-only queries remain allowed. Then plan from that state as a new decision; do not replay the earlier submission just because its result was uncertain.

The returned previews describe the settled state after this call, which is the starting state for a future batch; they do not predict that batch. Use interact for a listed available operation, including special game interfaces. References are semantic handles, not menu indices. select submits the complete final selection; a bundle is one option. When the native minimum is zero, submit select with refs=[] to decline all candidates and complete the selection. A positive minimum requires that many choices. Select only offered candidates and respect the required count. Each card reference identifies one actual card; use distinct references within one selection. A later action step may reuse a card reference if that same card is present and legal then. Costs may be numeric, X, explicitly no cost, or unknown and may use more than one resource. Unknown never means free. After all submitted steps finish, completed is returned even if the current state asks for another choice. If a role transition prevents an unexecuted step, the tail stops. Neither an action batch nor a stopped result rolls back prior effects. An optional top-level reason may briefly explain the choice for the whole batch. Use object names rather than temporary references. Do not provide a step-by-step reasoning transcript. The result does not echo this text.

For an action that needs a target, target may be omitted only when exactly one legal target exists when that step executes; the Mod binds it then. Multiple legal targets require an explicit reference. An explicitly supplied invalid target is never redirected. Omit target for actions that do not use one. Each potion reference identifies one actual bottle in the current map node. Slot movement does not change it. A consumed or discarded bottle loses its reference; a newly acquired bottle receives a new reference rather than reusing a retired one in that node. References may restart in the next node.

card.description: Observed card instance reference; an earlier step may move this card into hand.

target.description: For an action that needs a target, target may be omitted only when exactly one legal target exists when that step executes; the Mod binds it then. Multiple legal targets require an explicit reference. An explicitly supplied invalid target is never redirected. Omit target for actions that do not use one.

potion.description: Reference of the actual potion bottle in this node, not its slot or native definition ID.

target.description: For an action that needs a target, target may be omitted only when exactly one legal target exists when that step executes; the Mod binds it then. Multiple legal targets require an explicit reference. An explicitly supplied invalid target is never redirected. Omit target for actions that do not use one.

potion.description: Reference of the actual potion bottle in this node, not its slot or native definition ID.

action.description: Reference of a Mod-provided combat operation, including special game interfaces. It is bound to its semantic operation, not a changing menu position.

items.description: Use an exact supplied public reference, never a list index or an invented identifier.

refs.description: The complete final selection, not additions to the existing selection. Card, option, target, and bundle references are allowed when actual candidates allow them. Empty only when minimum is zero. A bundle reference selects that bundle as one option.

steps.description: Steps execute in array order. Structural validation occurs before any step; state-dependent legality is checked only when each step is reached.

reason.description: Optional short explanation of the game choice for this batch. Use object names, not temporary references; no step-by-step reasoning is needed.
